title: Adjustable Constrained Soft-Tissue Dynamics
venue: Pacific Graphics 2020 / Computer Graphics Forum, Vol. 39 (2020), No. 7
abstract: Constraint-based soft-tissue simulation suffers from an inherent coupling between vibration frequency and inertial amplitude — adjusting material properties cannot change them independently. The paper transforms the equations of motion into per-vertex non-inertial reference frames, scales the resulting fictitious (inertial) forces by a factor ε, then transforms back to the world frame. This yields a minimally modified equation of motion that lets animators independently control four salient visual characteristics of soft-tissue dynamics: vibration frequency, gravity sag, inertial amplitude, and damping decay time. Demonstrated on FEM characters with LBS+PSD geometric proxies.
